meaning: The number 62,000 has no established symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition.
description: The number 62,000 does not appear as a symbolically significant number in the Bible or in Jewish numerology (gematria). It may occur as part of larger numbers in census counts in the Old Testament, but it is not attributed any deeper symbolic or mystical meaning. In biblical number symbolism, simpler numbers like 7, 12, 40, and 70 carry established symbolic significance.

It may occur in census counts or listings in the Old Testament, such as in Numbers where the strength of the tribes is tallied, but it is not attributed any deeper symbolic or mystical meaning. In biblical number symbolism, simpler numbers like 7, 12, 40, and 70 carry established symbolic significance.
versions.reason: [minor] The description mentions that the number 'may occur in censuses' but is vague. Numbers 2:26 explicitly states 62,700 for the tribe of Dan, where 62,000 is the main part of this figure. It would strengthen the text to refer more precisely to this occurrence. But since it is actually 62,700 and not exactly 62,000, the current wording is acceptable.; [minor] The verse Numbers 2:26 mentions 62,700, not exactly 62,000. The description should clarify that the number appears as part of a larger figure (62,700) in the census of the tribe of Dan, to be accurate.

footnotes.text: In Numbers 2:26, the army of the tribe of Dan is given as 62,700 registered men, of which 62,000 make up the bulk of the number. This is part of the systematic census of the twelve tribes of Israel in the wilderness.
